Prevention: Nitrogen fertilizer late in the growing season.
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce splashing which spreads the disease.
Do not plant kale during wet season where possible.
Observe proper spacing of 60 x 60cm for proper aeration.
Ensure fields are clean by removing residues and destroy by burning or burying at a depth of 2 feet.
Apply mulch for moisture retention and to keep weeds out.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: beans, cabbage, carrot, cashew, cowpea, cucumber, eggplant, green gram, mango, okra, papaya, peas, peppers, pigeon pea, pumpkin, sesame, tomato, watermelon, wheat, zucchini/courgette.
Whitish spots of fungal growth on the upper leaf surface which coalesce and spread to the entire leaves and buds.
Look for the symptoms during wet weather seasons.
Take action when 5% of plants are infected.
Direct Control: Prune older leaves to reduce innoculum and increase air circulation.
